title: Portable Plugin Interface & Fallback Contract — scratch
content:
Purpose / context:
- Personal scratchpad for a lightweight, portable plugin (or extension) interface that can be used across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. I want a small, predictable contract so customers and internal teams can ship plugins (rerankers, external tool callers, privacy filters, telemetry enrichers) without coupling to runtime internals.

High-level goals:
- Minimal shape for plugin registration + invocation (JSON/HTTP friendly).
- Clear fallback semantics so runtime can gracefully degrade when plugin is slow/errored/unavailable.
- Configurable priority/timeout/retries on per-route or per-tenant basis.
- Observability hooks: traces, per-call latency, error category, invocation counts.
- Backwards-compatible: allow additional metadata fields but keep core contract stable.

Core concepts (quick):
- Plugin: logical extension with an ID, version, capabilities (sync/async, streaming, requires-kv).
- PluginHost: the runtime component that dispatches to plugin binary/endpoint (local sidecar, external webhook, third-party SaaS).
- RouteBinding: maps an API route or model call to a list of plugins + policies (timeout, priority, fallback action).
- Fallback action: how the platform behaves when plugin fails (ignore, use model-only path, local fallback plugin, synthetic stub).

Sequence (ASCII flow):
Client -> Redwood Runtime -> PluginHost -> [Plugin impl (local|remote)]
                |                           \\--fallback--> LocalFallbackPlugin
                |\
                \-observability -> tracing, metrics, debug payload

Lightweight registration schema (server-side config snippet):
{
  "plugin_id": "com.example.personalize-v1",
  "display_name": "Personalize Reranker (v1)",
  "capabilities": ["sync-rerank", "score-only"],
  "invocation": {
    "protocol": "http-json",
    "endpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:5001/invoke",
    "auth": {"type": "bearer", "token_ref": "secrets/personalize-token"}
  },
  "health_check": {"path": "/health", "interval_s": 10},
  "timeouts_ms": {"hard": 1200, "soft": 700},
  "priority": 10
}

Per-route binding example (policy):
{
  "route": "/v1/chat/completions",
  "model": "rw-13b-instruct",
  "plugins": [
    {"plugin_id": "com.example.personalize-v1", "binding": {"timeout_ms": 800, "fallback": "drop", "on_error": "log_and_continue"}},
    {"plugin_id": "redwood-local-slow-guard", "binding": {"timeout_ms": 200, "fallback": "use-synthetic"}}
  ]
}

Fallback semantics (draft):
- drop: silently drop plugin output and continue with model-only response. Metric: plugin.dropped.count / reason.
- use-synthetic: substitute plugin output with a synthesized, cheap heuristic (e.g., identity rerank).
- abort: abort the entire request and return a 5xx to client (only for critical plugins configured with abort).
- retry-without-plugin: if plugin is required for high-quality response but currently failing, reroute to preselected fallback model/variant that approximates behavior.

Error categorization (for metrics & decisions):
- transient-network: retryable (apply exponential backoff up to configured limit).
- auth-failure: non-retry, alert to infra/security teams.
- bad-response: plugin returned malformed payload (non-compliant schema). Treat as non-retryable; increment plugin.bad_response.
- overloaded / slow: treat as transient, but respect soft/hard timeouts.

Invocation request/response shapes (minimal; JSON):
Invocation request (from runtime -> plugin):
{
  "call_id": "uuid",
  "timestamp": "2025-03-04T15:22:01Z",
  "route": "/v1/chat/completions",
  "model": "rw-13b-instruct",
  "input": {"messages": [{"role":"user","content":"..."}]},
  "context_kv_refs": ["session:abc123:anchors"],
  "trace": {"trace_id":"t-...", "parent_span":"s-..."},
  "config": {"max_output_tokens": 64, "temperature": 0.0}
}

Minimal plugin response (success):
{
  "status": "ok",
  "plugin_output": {"reranked_indices": [0,2,1], "scores": [0.92,0.44,0.12]},
  "meta": {"elapsed_ms": 48}
}

Plugin error response (schema):
{
  "status": "error",
  "error_code": "overloaded",
  "message": "too many requests",
  "meta": {"suggested_retry_ms": 200}
}

Design notes on streaming plugins (optional):
- When plugin does streaming (e.g., content-moderation labels produced progressively), use an initial handshake that indicates streaming capability, then upgrade to chunked frames over an http/2+ SSE channel.
- Soft timeout applies to first-chunk latency; hard timeout applies to overall stream.
- If stream aborts mid-sequence, runtime must synthesize on-error frames so client gets valid JSON sequence end.

Local vs remote plugin hosting considerations:
- Local sidecar: low-latency, easier to guarantee soft timeouts. But more ops complexity for Private customers.
- Remote SaaS: easier to adopt but introduces network unreliability and auth surfaces. Need clear SLO expectations.

Observability contract (what runtime logs/metrics to emit):
- plugin.invocations.count{plugin_id,route,tenant}
- plugin.invocation.latency_ms{p95,p99}
- plugin.errors.count{error_code}
- plugin.fallbacks.count{fallback_type}
- plugin.bad_schema.count
- traces: include plugin.span with tags {plugin_id, elapsed_ms, status}

Testing / rollout checklist (personal):
- [ ] unit test harness for plugin mock server that can simulate transient errors, slow responses, malformed JSON.
- [ ] e2e with hosted runtime and a temporary sidecar to exercise soft/hard timeouts.
- [ ] chaos test: random 503s and slow responses to ensure fallback routes work and metrics look correct.
- [ ] security review on plugin auth scheme (token leakage possibilities).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should plugin invocation be synchronous only, or allow fire-and-forget async invocations for non-critical telemetry plugins? (pros: lower latency; cons: harder to guarantee delivery)
- How to version plugin interface without breaking private/on-prem customers? Maybe support v1/v2 Accept headers + graceful negotiation.
- Policy language: how expressive should per-route policies be? Small DSL or stick to a JSON object mapping? Start small.
- Do we want per-tenant quota on plugin calls (to prevent noisy neighbors)? Add to product backlog.

Small prototype API for graceful fallback (pseudocode):
- runtime calls plugin with timeout = binding.timeout_ms (soft)
- if plugin responds before soft timeout: use output
- if plugin doesn't respond by soft timeout but before hard timeout: return a "degraded" marker to model path and continue; track plugin.soft_timeout metric
- if no response by hard timeout: apply fallback action configured (drop|synthetic|abort) and increment plugin.hard_timeout

Notes to self (quick):
- Keep request/response minimal: large payloads are expensive; prefer ref by kv_ref for big context.
- Add small example plugin repo skeleton in GH (repo/plugins-sample) with README explaining contract.
- Discuss with infra: add a standard health-check path and auto-detect restart loops (backoff for plugin restarts).

References and tangents:
- Related infra ticket: JIRA INF-789 (plugin discovery + secrets).
- GH PR sketch: GH:repo/plugins-proposal#42 — contains earlier convo about streaming frames.
- Confluence: plugins/contract-v1 — central place for polished spec (this doc is scratch).

End of scratchpad. Will iterate into a short PR spec once checklist items pass manual tests.

-- Elena
